collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager apologized for ruining a neighbor's garden, but the neighbor wants it put right: help replant, or say sorry again.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) let (subject.his/her) pigs get into (friend)'s garden, and they ate everything. (subject) apologized at once. (friend) said that was nice, but sorry does not grow taro. (subject) feels (subject.he/she) has done (subject.his/her) part. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) spends a week digging, planting and building a proper fence for the pigs. (friend) watches, says nothing, and on the last day brings (subject.him/her) a cup of water. It is not friendship. But it is something.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) apologizes again, more warmly. (friend) shakes (friend.his/her) head and walks away. The garden stays bare until (friend) replants it alone. (subject) feels wronged. (friend) feels wronged. The pigs are perfectly happy.
